decisions.body:
Decision: option A, in the shape of design D1.

Verified your report against the code: resolveReadOnly/boardReader go through
TrackerAdapterFactory.create (TrackerWiring.java:142-158), the GitHub create
always runs GithubLabelProvisioner.provision (GithubTrackerAdapterFactory.java:123-124),
and provision lists then POSTs (GithubLabelProvisioner.java:58-81). One premise
is refuted: refuseForeignRef(SecretsProvider, TrackerConfig, TaskRef) already
is a read-only SPI default method with the credential seam, making one GET
through GithubForeignRepoCheck — so the SPI shape you proposed has a precedent,
and a default method is a compatible addition re-baselined under the japicmp
gate.

The change artifacts on this branch are already amended (uncommitted in the
worktree; commit them with your next round): design D3 now points to a new D7,
proposal gains an ADDED bullet, a sharper FR3, NG5 and the github-tracker
modified capability; the operator-doctor delta has the revised scenario
"Online adds a read-only tracker probe" plus a new "Online probe refused";
a new delta specs/tracker/github-tracker MODIFIES "Idempotent label
provisioning as startup smoke test" with the scenario "Read probe lists and
writes nothing"; task 3.3 is split into 3.3a-3.3c. Read D7 and the three tasks
first; the essentials:

1. 3.3a (:adapters:github): GithubLabelProvisioner.assess(owner, repo, labelDefs)
   makes the listing GET alone and returns a verdict — readable with the missing
   label names, or refused with the HTTP class and the cause the current message
   names (404 worded "not found or not visible to this token"; on 403 the
   X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions header verbatim). provision = assess, create
   the missing labels, refuse on a failed verdict, same exception and message.
   GithubLabelProvisionerSpec: provision refuses exactly when assess fails, over
   one data table of statuses; assess sends no POST.
2. 3.3b (:gnomish-plugin-api): default method
   TrackerAdapterFactory.probeRead(SecretsProvider, TrackerConfig) returning a
   probe verdict type of the api; the default makes no call and reports "not
   applicable" (the in-memory adapter keeps it); the GitHub override builds its
   client as refuseForeignRef does and returns assess. Regenerate the japicmp
   baseline in the same task.
3. 3.3c (:bootstrap): TrackerReadProbe over a TrackerWiring.probeRead relay
   (like refuseForeignRef), never create() or the read-only resolution. The line
   reports reading confirmed, the labels startup will create, and that write
   access is not verified (NG5: GitHub has no read-only way to evaluate a write).
   WireMock on a repository without the labels: exactly one GET and no POST with
   --online, no request without; plus the refused scenario (404 and 403).

Do not retry a 401 (GitHub locks the user out after repeated bad credentials);
the client already retries only 5xx/429/rate-limit, keep it so.

Task 5.4 is a human step: leave it unticked and note it in your report. Then
continue with 3.4 onward.

decisions.body:
Both blockers are resolved on the branch (commits 9e634b7b, 2ea9e7e3):
1. github-tracker delta split: "Read-only label probe" is an ADDED requirement, the MODIFIED one is back under 500 chars; the premature sync of the main specs was reverted — the archive round re-syncs them.
2. The seven pre-existing main specs were split by change split-long-spec-requirements, already synced and archived on this branch; `openspec validate --specs --strict` is 52/52 and `scripts/check-merged-specs.sh add-doctor-command` exits 0.
Continue with the archive stage.

lastEscalation.question:
Archive of add-doctor-command is blocked: `openspec validate --specs --strict --no-interactive` (openspec 1.14.1) cannot pass, for two reasons, and the archive stage forbids fixing either one by editing the delta or rewriting requirements it does not name.

State: all 4 artifacts done, 20/20 tasks ticked. Every delta header applies. I synced the four deltas into openspec/specs/ (uncommitted in the working copy; the change directory is NOT moved): tracker/github-tracker (MODIFIED 1), operator/operator-configuration (MODIFIED 1), git/git-transfer (MODIFIED 1), cli/operator-doctor (new main spec, ADDED 4). Each merged MODIFIED block is byte-identical to its delta block (diffed).

Blocker 1, caused by this change: openspec/changes/add-doctor-command/specs/tracker/github-tracker/spec.md, requirement 'Idempotent label provisioning as startup smoke test'. The delta's text (the paragraph before **Implements**) is 593 characters; the sentence added by D7 ('Provisioning SHALL be built on a non-refusing assessment ... the adapter's read-only probe SHALL be that assessment.') pushed it over OpenSpec's 500-character limit (.claude/rules/delta-specs.md, 'One behavior per requirement'). Strict validate now reports tracker/github-tracker as failed (requirements[3] text >500), which it did not at HEAD. A faithful merge cannot fix it; the delta must change through /opsx:update. What I would do: move the new sentence into a new ADDED requirement in the same delta, e.g. 'Read-only label probe' ('The adapter's read-only probe SHALL be the non-refusing listing assessment provisioning is built on ...', Implements FR3 of add-doctor-command), carrying the scenario 'Read probe lists and writes nothing' and the D7 note, and restore the MODIFIED block to the main text plus FR3 on its Implements line (or drop the MODIFIED block entirely). Note the scenario marker in the test then names the same title, so no test edit is needed if the title is kept.

Blocker 2, pre-existing and not caused by this change: at HEAD (before my merge, checked on a `git archive HEAD` copy) strict validate already fails 7 main specs on the same >500-character warning: build-system/quality-gates, cli/manual-run, lifecycle/task-branch-contract, observability/serve-observability, sandbox/execution-environment, serve/factory-serve, tracker/tracker-take. The archive stage may edit only capabilities this change has deltas for, so these cannot be fixed here; the verify check 'openspec validate --specs --strict must pass' will fail on them whatever this change does. They need their own change (split the long requirements), or the stage check must tolerate warnings that predate the branch.
options: Fix blocker 1 via /opsx:update on add-doctor-command (split the github-tracker requirement as described), and handle the 7 pre-existing specs in a separate change; then re-run archive
Archive anyway: accept the >500-character warnings for now (github-tracker included) and relax/skip the strict-validate check for this round
